extracted.intended_audience: Renaissance courtiers; readers of conduct literature; students of Castiglione
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance for how a courtier (especially an older/mature one) should experience and govern love: avoid sensual excesses, cultivate rational/divine love, and conduct oneself honorably toward the beloved. The text lays out stages of loving thought (sensual → rational → universal → divine) and practical behaviors for the lover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrain sense with the bridle of reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrain the perversity of sense with the bridle of reason; reason should govern appetite and senses so the soul is not led astray by bodily vigour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bembo repeatedly argues that reason must control sense, especially in maturer age: mature persons can love guided by rational choice, and restraining appetite preserves the graces and benefits of true love. The text contrasts youth (led by sense) with the old (who can more easily use reason as a bridle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandon sensual love in maturer years
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensual love may be excused in youth, but those who remain inflamed by sensual desire in old age are blameworthy and should abandon such appetites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While sensual love in youth can lead to some good acts and be partially excused, the text insists that older men who preserve appetite and subject reason to sense deserve blame and 'perpetual infamy among the unreasoning animals.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Early intervention when passion arises
rubrics_metrics.description: At the first stage of being inflamed by beauty, one must provide a speedy cure: arouse reason, arm the heart's fortress, and shut the way to sense and appetite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the flame is extinguished early by reason, danger passes; if it survives or grows, the lover must wholly shun vulgar love and enter the path of divine/rational love.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enjoy beauty chiefly by sight and hearing (ministers of reason)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty should be enjoyed primarily through the eyes and the hearing—senses that minister to reason—rather than by touch or other appetites that incline toward the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bembo explains that beauty is incorporeal and that touch cannot properly enjoy it; the lover should feed his soul with the splendour of the lady's aspect, voice, words, and music, thereby avoiding unseemly bodily appetite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor, obey, and prefer the lady's convenience; love mind as well as body
rubrics_metrics.description: Obey, please, and honour the beloved with reverence; prefer her convenience and pleasures to one's own, and value the beauty of mind at least as much as that of body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Courtier should show reverence and regard for the lady's inner qualities; by esteeming her mind and cultivating her virtue, the relationship becomes more virtuous and harmonious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate virtue in the beloved through admonition and counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek by admonition and good advice to lead the beloved toward modesty, temperance, and true chastity; 'sow virtue' in her mind so that fair behaviour is the fruit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By cultivating the lady's moral qualities, the lover ensures that their mutual wishes are virtuous and that she will be obedient, sweet, and affable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kissing as a chaste joining of souls in rational love
rubrics_metrics.description: A kiss may be permitted within rational (divine) love because it is the union of soul rather than merely of body; it can be chaste when intended as spiritual communion, not to arouse unseemly desire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bembo contrasts this with sensual rules that forbid kissing: in rational love the mouth is an instrument of the soul (words, breath), and the kiss symbolizes the pouring of souls into one another rather than bodily appetite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internalize beauty to avoid torment of absence
rubrics_metrics.description: To escape the suffering of absence, turn desire from the particular body to beauty itself and fashion it in the imagination apart from matter; thus carry the beloved's beauty within the heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By internalizing and purifying the beloved's beauty (imagining it apart from materiality), the lover is freed from jealousy, suspicion, and the anguish that follows absence; imagination can even make the beloved more beautiful inwardly than outwardly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascend from particular to universal beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than fixating on the beauty of one body, the lover should collect and combine many particulars in thought to form an idea of universal human beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stage reduces the multitude of particular beauties to the unity of a single universal concept; it is a noble stage (few attain) but still limited because imagination remains a corporeal faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press onward from imagination to the intellect toward divine beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: After attaining a universal concept of beauty, the lover should turn inward to contemplate the beauty seen by the 'eyes of the mind' and then ascend to intellectual and finally divine vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bembo describes the highest stage where the soul, purged by philosophy and spiritual practice, perceives angelic/divine beauty, unites with the intellect, and enjoys supreme felicity beyond sense and reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid violent, dishonorable or self-destructive responses to love
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-governed lover will not resort to jealousies, suspicions, assaults (upon the woman or others), self-harm, or infamy upon the beloved; he should preserve honour in conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By internalizing love and rising to rational stages, the lover avoids extremes (beating women, suicide, defamation) that arise from sensual passion and lead to ruin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensual love in youth may be excused if it produces gentleness and worth
rubrics_metrics.description: Although sensual love is intrinsically evil, in youth it can be excused insofar as it prompts youths to worthy acts (gentleness, courtesy, worth) and eventually leads them to perceive their error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text allows a measured leniency for youthful frailty provided the lover shows noble qualities and abandons sensual love by maturer age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat outward beauty as a sign of inward goodness but beware deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Outward beauty is generally a token of inward goodness—'beauty springs from God'—yet the senses can deceive and fair looks may mask cruelty or vice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bembo notes physiognomy and examples (beautiful yet cruel women, beautiful men who are wicked) and warns against assuming beauty guarantees virtue; sometimes poor training or external causes corrupt the beautiful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not ascribe the world's evils to beauty itself
rubrics_metrics.description: Many evils (hatreds, wars, destructions) that seem connected to beauty arise from immoderate appetites of men, not from beauty per se; beauty tends toward goodness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues that beauty, like the order of nature and art, reflects goodness; to blame beauty for human appetites' consequences is mistaken—the remedies lie in curbing appetite and reasoned conduct.
